correctness.rationale: For all L>=2, k>=2, integer 1<=s<=floor(k/2), and 1<=j<L, exactly one active hyperedge is maintained. The two indexed front types have R_j -> R_(j+1) with probability s/k, R_j -> V_j otherwise, V_j -> V_(j-1) with probability s/k, V_j -> R_j otherwise; boundary states are absorbing. At every transient state the active group rings at rate 1. Direct substitution solves the coupled mean-time recurrences with U_j=(L-j)+((k-s)/s)j(L-j), V_j=j+((k-s)/s)j(L-j). Strictly positive absorption paths imply finite mean and uniqueness. Count of A voters is a bounded martingale, yielding fixation probability [j(k-s)+s]/[L(k-s)+s]. 336 exact labeled absorbing-chain computations independently reproduce both formulas and verify reachable states, including k=2s. The computation is finite corroboration, not the infinite-family proof.

originality.rationale: The inspected open-access original 2024 full text gives the proportional group-update mechanism and simulations with closure; it does not prove a single-front invariant hyperpath reduction or an exact group-count/overlap-dependent mean hitting time. The inspected 2022 full preprint uses majority-influence rules, and Chung--Tsiatas treat general hypergraph random walks, chiefly memoryless and partially memoryless spectral bounds. Exact formula searches returned no covering claim. Standard Markov-chain and martingale tools, as well as qualitative quadratic group-count scaling in related language-contact models, are prior work and not claimed as new. Scope of novelty is the specified closed-form, physically normalized hyperpath result, not absolute priority.
residual_risks: No exhaustive historical mathematical-literature search; direct-but-unindexed or differently phrased formulas may exist.
Kim et al. 2024 preprint was checked by abstract only, though its distinct update rule reduces direct overlap likelihood.
The general Markov-chain methods of earlier work can in principle evaluate any finite instance, but no directly dominating closed L,k,s,j identity was found.
Only the polarized-front invariant class and no-rewiring clock are covered; no claim for all colorings.

value.rationale: Finite-size metastability and influence of group geometry are central questions for proportional polyadic opinion spreading (Golovin--Mölter--Kuehn). On an arbitrary-length genuine overlapping group path with a polarized interface, the reduction stays finite-dimensional, and the precise waiting time has a quadratic L^2 term with sharp inverse-overlap factor (k-s)/s. This resolves a natural initial-condition/bottleneck problem at all admissible integer sizes, gives a neutral fixation benchmark, and distinguishes structural delay from mean-field estimates. A natural complete parametric first-passage classification, not arbitrary numerical slice.
